notes:
Independent review by Claude Code, session cc-fb70e5, 23 September 2026, of the extraction by session cc-442dc5 (issue #1462). cc-fb70e5 appears nowhere in it.

Provenance. All three artifacts the extraction records were re-downloaded and all three hashes match byte for byte: the arXiv v3 PDF 285f7d20...9c4e072a, the v3 e-print ff989b40...262b5aa4 (integralpadicHodge.tex, 5932 lines) and the open-access published PDF on Centre Mersenne a924d36c...52702bb. The locators' published page numbers are therefore checkable, and were checked against both texts.

Numbering and coverage. All theorem environments share one per-section counter. Simulating that independently gives 237 numbered objects, exactly the count the extraction reports, and 229 appear in an item locator. The eight that do not are all remarks and none is a gap: Remark 14.2, the only one with mathematical content (Theorem C needs only that C be perfectoid with all p-power roots of unity), is folded verbatim into every Theorem 14.1 item's statement and cited there by number; the other seven are introductory commentary, history, an open question and example commentary.

Statuses. Both library items were opened at Mathlib 082e2d3: PreTilt (RingTheory/Perfection.lean:634), WittVector (RingTheory/WittVector/Defs.lean:52) and, in RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean, fontaineTheta (165) and fontaineTheta_teichmuller (182) inside namespace WittVector, and surjective_fontaineTheta (195), which falls after that namespace closes at line 190 and is therefore correctly cited with no namespace. The 92 planned items cite 27 layers, all of which exist, concentrated in AInfCohomology AI.1-AI.5, the roadmap whose descriptions name BMS1 as their source.

Routes. All fourteen are source routes and all are accepted. The extraction's judgement is that the atlas already owns this paper's mathematics, and it holds up: every cited layer exists in data/atlas.json, every stage belongs to the roadmap that claims it, and ten of the fourteen layer descriptions name BMS1 or its authors explicitly (AI.0-AI.5, CP.3, CP.5, CR.3, CR.4). The four that do not - AI.7, R07.4, P8 and PerfectoidQuotients Q0:integral-algebra - own the Breuil-Kisin cohomology, Breuil-Kisin modules, relative period sheaves and integral perfectoid algebra that their routed items need.

Mistakes in the paper. All 18 were checked at their locators in both the TeX and the published PDF and all 18 are confirmed; all are typographical and affect nothing. Several were settled by the paper against itself: the differential printed with g y where the display two lines above has g x (E7); eta_{phi(mu)} where the two neighbouring lines establish eta_mu (E13); AOmega_r against the AOmega_R of the display above (E18); Theorem 9.4(iii) cited for what its part (ii) states (E8); and E17, where the proof discusses parts (i), (ii) and (iii) of a proposition that has exactly two. E11 is a composite of five stray A's in a section that writes its base ring as S fifty-four times. E3 records a second slip in the same sentence that its correction does not mention - a plural 'modules' - which this review notes, and its substance is confirmed: the map f is never given a name, the paper introducing it only as 'the map S -> A_inf that sends T to [pi^flat]^p'.

Nothing was corrected in place: every locator resolves, every quotation is accurate, and no item, status or route needed changing.

Verdict: accept.
